title: Prompt Worklet Garden — personal brainstorm
body:
Scratchpad / seed notes for an idea: 'Prompt Worklet Garden'

Goal: build a lightweight, composable library of small prompt components ("worklets") that product teams can assemble at runtime or at build time to produce higher-quality, cheaper, and more maintainable prompts. Think: UI components but for prompts.

Motivation: prompts are messy—lots of copy-paste, subtle ordering bugs, duplicate schema validation, hard to iterate. If we standardize small, testable building blocks (instructions, examples, extractors, persona snippets, safety filters), teams can:
- Reuse proven patterns across features
- Measure and A/B worklets instead of monolithic prompts
- Autoswap cheaper paraphrases or quantized model variants for certain worklets
- Enable product-level governance (safety + legal approved worklets)

Core concepts (working):
- Worklet: atomic prompt fragment with metadata (type, inputs, outputs, cost-hint, quality-tag).
- Worklet pack: collection/versioned set (namespace) teams can pin.
- Composer: runtime that expands a composition spec into final prompt and manages placeholders. Could be server-side (Redwood) or client-side in SDK.
- Runtime directives: hints like max_tokens, prefer_short_examples, fallbacks, model-affinity.
- Local testing harness: small evals for worklets to check hallucination/formatting for a given model.

API sketch (ideas):
- POST /v1/worklet/compose {pack: "sales-qa/v1", composition: ["persona:concise", "instruction:answer", {"examples": "fewshot:order"}], inputs: {user_q: "..."}} -> returns expanded prompt / tokens estimate / cost-estimate
- SDK: WorkletRegistry.load('team/foo:latest').compose(spec, inputs)
- Console: Worklet browser with approved tag, last-eval, examples, and quick A/B playground

User stories (rough):
- As a PM, I want to pick a verified 'safety-filter' worklet so my assistant never outputs PII on exports. Acceptance: filter triggers X tests in harness and blocked content is redacted.
- As an engineer, I want to swap the 'long-form-examples' worklet with 'concise-examples' to reduce token cost by ~30% without significant drop in task success. Acceptance: metric compare (task success delta < 5%, cost down > 20%).
- As a compliance reviewer, I want a list of worklets used in a rollout with their approval status and changelog. Acceptance: audit export with worklet ids + pack pinned.

Operational: telemetry we need
- Worklet reuse rate (# calls using any worklet / total prompt calls)
- Median tokens per worklet and per composed prompt
- Rolling task success by worklet id (via eval datasets / customer-provided test sets)
- Failure modes: malformed composition, placeholder mismatch, unsafe substitution

Experiments to run (priority):
1) A/B single-worklet swap for a live feature: replace heavy example block with summary-style example pack. Track cost and end-to-end task success for 2 weeks.
2) Server vs client composition: measure extra latency and 95th percentile; caching benefit if composed server-side and cached per user-context.
3) Versioned pack staging: canary 5% of traffic to new pack, automatic rollback if latency/cost degrade or eval metrics drop.

Design/UX notes:
- Console: searchable garden with filters (approved, experimental, cost-hint, last-updated, owner). Preview expands sample inputs to show final prompt and estimated tokens.
- Editor: mini-DSL for placeholders e.g. {{user.name}} with type hints; linting shows type mismatch.
- Inline docs: every worklet has example inputs/outputs, unit tests, linked evals.

Engineering concerns / constraints:
- KV cache interference: if worklets change context prefix shapes, could break KV cache reuse. Need kernel for similarity-aware cache keys or hash-stable placeholder encoding.
- Batching: need to ensure composed prompts still play nicely with batching and continuous cache reuse. Longer composed prompts reduce throughput; consider 'inline references' where worklet stored server-side and id passed to runtime to reduce token count. But then runtime would have to expand server-side before sending to model (adds latency).
- Security: worklets may include sensitive phrasing; enforce ACLs, audits, per-pack visibility. Worklet packs for enterprise can be private (stored in private deployments).
- Storage size: many small packs -> indexing and GC policy. Keep canonical cache for latest pinned version.

Open questions / risks:
- Who owns the quality metric for a worklet? Product team or platform? Maybe both: platform owns basic safety and syntactic correctness; product team owns task success.
- Should a worklet be purely declarative (assembler) or can it contain control flow (if/else) + small script? Scripting increases power but also complexity and security surface. Start declarative.
- How to measure composition-level regressions (emergent behavior) where each worklet is fine in isolation but combined causes problems? Need combinatorial regression tests or conservative rollout.

Minimum viable scope (MVP):
- Worklet schema + storage with versioning (private + shared packs)
- Simple composer that concatenates fragments with placeholder substitution and token estimate output
- Console list UI + pack pinning + canary toggle
- One live experiment (example-swap) with telemetry and rollback

Backlog ideas (parking lot):
- Worklet marketplace (internal): teams can publish and rate worklets
- Parametric worklets: small templates that accept scoring knobs (verbosity=0.3)
- Auto-suggest worklets when editing prompts via LLM-based recommendations
- Worklet-level quantization hints (prefer 8-bit for cheap-ish completions)

Immediate next actions (for me):
- Draft short PRD (1 page) focusing on MVP + experiment plan (deadline 2025-02-15)
- Sync with Maya (ux) and Ivy (runtime) next Tue — bring sketch of console list and API shape
- Create JIRA epic PWG-1 and wire basic telemetry events (worklet.used, worklet.composed_tokens)

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Example simple schema: {id, name, type, pack, version, body, placeholders:[{name,type}], cost_hint, owner, approved}
- Think about canonicalization: store compiled form (escaped placeholders) to avoid ambiguity across models with different tokenizers
- If server-side expansion, add short expansion cache TTL keyed by (pack, version, placeholder-hash)

References / links to check next:
- look at 'snippet libraries' in other products (Google Dialogflow snippets?), internal "prompt snippets" notes (I suspect there's overlap)
- check infra constraints with SRE (latency budget for composition)

Roughly fleshed but messy — intended as my personal playground for the PRD. Will refine into a one-pager and then a tracked epic.
